Note:
Aamon is a magic?damage assassin who excels at picking off isolated targets with burst combos from camouflage. His kit revolves around building armor charges and Soul Shards, entering Camouflage to become untargetable and highly mobile, then collapsing onto a target with Slayer Shards and Endless Shards to deal massive damage that scales with the enemy’s lost HP. With strong self?sustain from Invisible Armor and high mobility, Aamon can weave in and out of fights, dodging key skills while setting up lethal all?ins.

Aamon works best in lineups that can provide vision, crowd control, or soft setup so he can safely enter Camouflage and choose the right moment to strike. When paired with tanks, supports, or mages that can lock enemies down or chip them low first, Aamon can quickly finish off priority backline targets and reset fights. In the right composition, he functions as a slippery execution assassin who punishes overextended or poorly positioned carries
Basic Attack Description:
Aamon enters the Camouflage state each time he hits an enemy with a skill, during which he cannot be targeted, recovers 25 (+15% Total Magic Power) plus 3% of his lost HP every 0.5s, and gains 80% extra Movement Speed that rapidly decays over 3s.
Upon leaving the Camouflage state, Aamon immediately resets his Basic Attack's cooldown and enhances his Basic Attacks within the next 3s. Each enhanced Basic Attack deals 70 (+100% Total Physical Attack) (+115% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage. The first attack after actively leaving Camouflage is enhanced to deal 84 (+120% Total Physical Attack) (+138% Total Magic Power) damage and reduces all skill cooldowns by 1s.
Skill 1 Description:
Passive: Aamon charges his armor through enhanced Basic Attacks or while camouflaged. At 5 charges, Aamon throws 6 shards at the target on his next attack, each shard dealing 50 (+15% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage. The shards will then scatter around the target.

Active: Aamon throws a shard at a nearby enemy, dealing 175 (+60% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage.
Skill 2 Description:
Aamon throws a shard forward, dealing 120 (+50% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemies along the way. The shard will return to Aamon after a short delay and allow him to enter the Camouflage state.
If the shard hits a non-minion enemy, it'll slow them by 50% for 2s and return to Aamon immediately.
Skill 4 Description:
Aamon throws all shards at a designated enemy and slows them by 30% for 1.5s. After a short delay, the shards will fly to the enemy's location again, each dealing 90 (+24% Total Magic Power)-150 (+40% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage.

The number of shards increases with Aamon's armor charges and the shards on the ground (8-25).
The damage dealt increases with the target's lost HP, to the max when the target's HP is below 30%. The same target takes less damage from subsequent attacks.

Akai is a durable tank who specializes in crowd control, disruption, and peeling rather than pure damage. His kit revolves around using Body Slam and Headbutt to slow, knock back, and reposition enemies, then locking them into walls or unfavorable spots with Heavy Spin. Thanks to his high base durability and strong zoning, Akai can safely front line, protect his carries, and break enemy formations during key objectives or tower defenses.

Akai works best with lineups that can quickly follow up on his displacement and control, such as burst mages, marksmen, or fighters that benefit from enemies being pinned or separated. When paired with reliable follow?up damage, his ult can isolate priority targets, deny enemy engages, and create huge space for his backline to freely deal damage. In the right composition, Akai acts as both a primary engager and a powerful anti?dive tool that punishes careless positioning.
Basic Attack Description:
Akai gains a 25 (+5% Total HP) shield for 4s on each skill cast and marks enemy heroes and Creeps hit by his skills.

Akai's Basic Attacks deal 25 (+5% Total HP) extra Physical Damage to marked enemies.
Skill 1 Description:
Akai charges in the target direction, dealing 300 (+50% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies along the way. If Akai hits an enemy hero during this process, he'll knock them airborne for 0.5s and be able to roll in the Joystick's direction once.

Akai can cast Headbutt during Heavy Spin to quickly adjust his position.
Skill 2 Description: Akai smashes the ground with his body, dealing 270 (+6% Total HP) Physical Damage to nearby enemies and slowing them by 45% for 2s.
Skill 4 Description:
Akai removes all debuffs on him and spins for 4s, gaining Slow Immunity while continuously dealing 100 (+50% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back. Enemy heroes knocked back will knock back other heroes they collide with during the process.

Akai also gradually increases his Movement Speed by 70% over the duration. This skill can only be interrupted by Suppression.

Alice is a tank/mage who excels at diving into the heart of team fights, sustaining herself through continuous healing, and dealing persistent AoE magic damage. Her kit revolves around stacking Crimson to trigger Blood Banquet, which lets her drain HP from nearby enemies while gaining movement speed and turning extended fights in her favor. With Crimson Gleam and Doom Waltz, she can both engage and reposition aggressively, combining mobility, burst, and slows to stick to priority targets or escape after a short trade.

Alice fits best in drafts that want a durable front?line mage who scales with time and thrives in drawn?out 5v5s. She pairs well with engage tanks and crowd?control supports who can lock enemies inside her AoE damage and give her time to ramp up Blood Banquet. In coordinated fights around tight spaces or objectives, her ultimate, Throne of Ruin, can massively swing team fights by combining damage, HP scaling, and control immunity. However, she is vulnerable to strong burst before she builds enough HP or stacks, and she can struggle against heavy anti?heal. When played around proper scaling, flank angles, and team CC, Alice becomes a hard?to?kill battle mage who slowly overwhelms teams through sustain and repeated AoE nukes.
Basic Attack Description:
When Alice's skills hit, she gains 1 stack(s) of Crimson, lasting 4s. Once Crimson reaches 2 stacks, Blood Banquet activates, dealing 25 (+30% Total Magic Power) plus 0.5%-2.5% of the target's Max HP (scales with level) as Magic Damage to nearby units (hitting heroes with skills refreshes the duration) and recovering 10 (+3% Extra Max HP) HP for Alice every 0.5s.
While Blood Banquet is active, Alice gains 8% Movement Speed. Blood Banquet can deal up to 70(+10*Hero Level) Magic Damage to creeps.
Skill 1 Description: Alice fires blood energy forward, dealing 100 (+50% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage. Before the blood energy dissipates, this skill can be cast again to activate Scarlet Shadow, allowing Alice to blink to the blood energy's location.
Skill 2 Description: Alice performs a deadly dance, dealing 350 (+130% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to nearby enemies and slowing them by 70% for 1s. If Blood Banquet is active at this time, it also scorches enemies, dealing 300% of Blood Banquet's damage and healing Alice for the same amount.
Skill 4 Description:
Alice surrounds herself with blood, gaining Control Immunity and 50% Damage Reduction while slowing herself by 50%. After 1.5s, she descends with force, dealing 500 (+150% Total Magic Power) (+20% Extra Max HP) Magic Damage to all enemies in range and immobilizing them for 1s.
While charging her Ultimate, Alice can only use Scarlet Shadow.

Alpha is a fighter who excels in extended skirmishes and follow?up engages rather than pure frontline tanking. His kit revolves around charging into fights, dealing sustained physical damage over time, and chasing priority targets that have already been controlled by his teammates.

Alpha works best when paired with heroes that can reliably start fights or lock enemies in place, such as Atlas, Vexana, or Selena. With strong crowd control and setup from his team, Alpha can consistently land his skill combos, stick to his targets, and quickly shred even tankier opponents. He prefers lineups where he can enter second, clean up fights, and punish enemies that overcommit or get caught by hard CC
Basic Attack Description:
When Alpha uses a skill, Beta will be summoned to attack. Enemies that are hit by Beta 2 time(s) will be Locked On.

Locked On: After Alpha deals damage to the target, Beta will fire a laser at them, dealing 80 (+80% Extra Physical Attack) (+8*Hero Level) True Damage and briefly applying a powerful slow effect.
This skill only deals 75% damage to Creeps.
Skill 1 Description:
Alpha unleashes an energy wave in the target direction, dealing 100 (+90% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies in its path and slowing them by 40% for 1s.

Beta then strafes enemies along the same path, dealing 60 (+30% Extra Physical Attack) True Damage.
Skill 2 Description:
After a short delay, Alpha swings his blade in the target direction, dealing 180 (+100% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies in a fan-shaped area and restoring 40 (+30% Extra Physical Attack) HP for each enemy hit.

Beta then strafes enemies in the same area, dealing 60 (+30% Total Physical Attack) True Damage.
Skill 4 Description:
Beta dives to the target location, dealing 100 (+20% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies hit and stunning them for 1s. Alpha then leaps towards the same location, knocking enemies in his path airborne and carrying them to the landing location. Alpha then slams down, dealing 250 (+100% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage and slowing the enemies by 40% for 1.5s.

Beta then attacks the same area 5 times, dealing 15 (+30% Extra Physical Attack) True Damage each time.

Note: Alucard is a physical fighter–assassin who focuses on diving into the enemy backline and sustaining through lifesteal while dealing heavy damage in close range. His kit rewards staying on top of targets and chaining abilities to amplify his basic attacks, allowing him to quickly eliminate squishy heroes once he finds a good angle. With sufficient farm and items, Alucard can quickly snowball and become very hard to duel in 1v1 or small skirmishes. However, he is vulnerable to crowd control, kiting, and burst damage that can stop his lifesteal from keeping him alive. Alucard works best with teammates who provide reliable engage, lockdown, or peel so he can safely enter fights, stick to priority targets, and avoid being focused before he can deal his full damage
Basic Attack Description:
After each skill cast, Alucard's next Basic Attack allows him to dash to the target's location and deal (+125% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage.
Demon Hunter: Alucard deals 10% extra damage to Creeps.
Skill 1 Description: Alucard rolls to the target location and slams his blade on the ground, dealing 270 (+85% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies hit and slowing them by 40% for 2s.
Skill 2 Description: Alucard launches a whirling slash, dealing 345 (+120% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to nearby enemies.
Skill 4 Description:
Passive: Alucard permanently gains 10% Hybrid Lifesteal.
Active: Alucard absorbs the energy of enemies in the target area, reducing their Movement Speed by 30% and Hybrid Defense by 10. Alucard gains 10 Hybrid Defense for each enemy hero hit, and reduces the cooldown of his other skills to 50% for 6s.
Use Again: Alucard releases a shockwave in the target direction, dealing 400 (+200% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies hit.

Angela is a pure support hero who specializes in shielding, healing, and amplifying her allies’ impact rather than dealing damage herself. Her kit revolves around poking and slowing enemies with Love Waves, providing shields and movement speed through Heartguard, and using Puppet?on?a?String to root enemies after a delay. With her global ultimate, Angela can jump onto an allied hero anywhere on the map, granting them a large shield and access to her skills, allowing her to join fights instantly and turn losing skirmishes around.

Angela works best with aggressive frontliners or hypercarries who want to dive deep, such as fighters and assassins that benefit from extra sustain and crowd control. When paired with heroes like Alpha, Thamuz, or other hard?engage initiators, she can keep them alive during risky dives, help them stick to targets with slows and roots, and provide constant sustain throughout extended fights. In the right lineup, Angela enables high?tempo plays, cross?map rotations, and clutch saves that make it very difficult for the enemy team to punish overextensions.
Basic Attack Description: Angela gains 7.5% extra Movement Speed for 4s each time she casts a skill (up to 30%). When she's attached to an allied hero, the Movement Speed boost is transferred to the allied hero.
Skill 1 Description:
Angela sends Love Waves in the target direction, dealing 170 (+80% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemies hit, revealing their positions briefly, and applying a stack of Lover's Mark (up to 5 stacks). Each stack of Lover's Mark increases the damage by 20% and slows enemies hit by 8% for 3s.

Love Waves also restore 150 (+75% Total Magic Power) HP to allied heroes hit. Angela can store up to 5 charges of this skill and the recharge time is affected by Cooldown Reduction.
Skill 2 Description:
Angela launches a Puppet String at the target enemy(excluding minions), dealing 300 (+40% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage and gradually slowing them by up to 80%. If the enemy is still connected to the string after 3s, they'll be immobilized for 1.5s and dealt 450 (+60% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage. 

Each stack of Lover's Mark increases the final damage by 20%.
Skill 4 Description: Angela begins channeling, applying a 600 (+150% Total Magic Power) shield that lasts 6s to the target allied hero regardless of distance. After the channeling is complete, she attaches herself to the allied hero for 12s, during which she can cast skills at zero Mana cost. Angela can cast this skill again to cancel the channeling or detach herself from the allied hero. The attaching state will end early if the allied hero is killed.

Argus is a late?game fighter who thrives in extended fights and clutch skirmishes thanks to his self?sustain, mobility, and pseudo?immortality. His kit revolves around building Malice Energy to empower his Basic Attacks and skills, letting him dash in, stick to targets, and deal high single?target damage while healing himself. With Demonic Grip and Meteoric Sword, Argus can close gaps, lock enemies down, and chase along Cursed Trails, turning otherwise lost chases into secured kills.

Argus shines in drafts that want a hard?to?kill side?laner or backline diver who becomes more threatening the longer a fight lasts. His ultimate, Eternal Evil, makes him extremely difficult to burst down, allowing him to dive deep, absorb cooldowns, and then convert his damage dealt into HP if he survives the duration. He pairs well with engage or peel supports that can help him reach priority targets and keep him fighting during his ultimate. However, Argus is vulnerable to hard crowd control when his ultimate is down and can be kited by high?mobility ranged carries, so he requires good timing, flanking angles, and matchup awareness to fully unlock his carry potential
Basic Attack Description:
When Argus' Meteoric Sword reaches 100 Malice Energy, he will launch a Demonic Slash with his next Basic Attack, dealing 180 (+80% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage and recovering 150 (+10% Total Physical Attack) HP. This attack ignores 40% of the target's Physical Defense.
Argus' Meteoric Sword gains 5 Malice Energy per second and 10 Energy per Basic Attack (critical strikes grant an additional 10 Energy).
Skill 1 Description:
Argus stretches out a demonic hand in the target direction, dealing 125 (+60% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to the first enemy hero or Creep hit, stunning them for 0.7s, and pulling him and the target towards each other. If no enemy is hit, Argus pulls himself toward the hand's destination instead.
Use Again: Argus dashes and strikes in the target direction, dealing 175 (+100% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies along the path.
Skill 2 Description:
After a short delay, Argus thrusts his Meteoric Sword in the target direction, dealing 120 (+100% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies hit (200% damage against minions) and reducing their Movement Speed by 80% for 0.8s. The delay time decreases as Argus's Attack Speed increases. Enemy heroes hit will be Cursed for 4s, during which they leave a Cursed Trail behind. Argus gains 20% Movement Speed while on a Cursed Trail.
Meteoric Sword damage counts as Basic Attack damage and can trigger Attack Effects. Hitting heroes restores 100 Malice Energy (excess is preserved).
Skill 4 Description:
Argus removes all debuffs on himself, dealing 150 (+50% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to nearby enemies and becoming the Fallen Angel for 4s (hitting heroes enhances Warmonger). Fallen Angel: Gains 40% Movement Speed that decays over 1s; when the transformation ends, he converts all his damage dealt in the Fallen Angel state into HP. If he takes fatal damage in the Fallen Angel state, the duration of the Movement Speed boost will be reset, and he will gain Death Immunity for 4s. Enhanced Warmonger: Demonic Slash grants 50 Malice Energy (50 extra Malice Energy with critical hits).
If Death Immunity isn't triggered, the cooldown will be reduced by 50%.

Arlott is a fighter/assassin hybrid who excels at punishing clumped enemies and turning crowd control into burst windows. His kit revolves around Demon Gaze marking controlled targets, then dashing and comboing through them with Vengeance and empowered skills for high single?target and multi?target damage. With good spacing, Arlott can repeatedly weave in and out of fights, using his mobility and resets to chase, reposition, or escape after a quick pick.

Arlott fits best in drafts that have reliable crowd control or knock?ups to help him consistently trigger Demon Gaze and line up big Final Slash angles. He synergizes well with tanks and mages that can group enemies together, letting him cleave through multiple targets and swing team fights with a single ultimate. However, he is vulnerable to hard point?and?click CC and can struggle into heavy peel or kite comps if he can’t find flanks. When drafted with good engage and setup, Arlott becomes a high?tempo skirmisher and team?fight cleaner who thrives in chaotic, clustered fights
Basic Attack Description:
Arlott possesses a demonic eye that will Mark enemy units near Arlott that become affected by control effects for 7s.
The eye will also automatically Mark a nearby enemy hero in vision every 7s.
Skill 1 Description: Arlott swings his lance forward, dealing 200 (+60% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage and briefly stunning targets in an area. Targets hit by the farther part of the AOE will be stunned for 1s instead.
Skill 2 Description:
Arlott charges at an enemy, dealing 135 (+60% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage (this skill cannot be interrupted during movement).
If Arlott's target is Marked, he gains a brief burst of Movement Speed, and this skill will deal double damage, immediately refresh its cooldown, and recover 70 (+60% Total Physical Attack) HP to Arlott (only restores 50% of that amount when used on a non-hero unit).
Skill 4 Description:
Passive: Each level-up reduces Demon Gaze's interval by 1s.
Active: Arlott cleaves in front of him, dealing 400 (+80% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to targets in the area while pushing them to the end of the AOE and briefly revealing their location (this skill can only be interrupted by Suppression).

Note: Atlas is a Tank hero with strong crowd control abilities. His kit revolves around his unique Mecha Sentry mechanic, which allows him to enter an Ejected State for increased mobility and damage reduction. His skills provide excellent initiation potential with multiple crowd control effects including slows, freezes, and stuns. Atlas excels at disrupting enemy formations and protecting his team with his defensive capabilities and control effects.
Basic Attack Description:
Atlas generates Frigid Breath around him for 5s each time he casts a skill. Enemies affected by Frigid Breath will have their Movement Speed gradually reduced over 2s, after which they'll be frozen for 0.5s.

Atlas gains 20 (+0.5% Extra Max HP) extra Physical & Magic Defense when Frigid Breath is present.
Skill 1 Description:
Atlas smashes the ground and causes 3 explosions. Each explosion deals 215 (+60% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemies.
Ejected State: If Atlas is ejected from his Mecha Sentry, both he and his Mecha will cast Annihilate.
Skill 2 Description:
Atlas enters Ejected State, gaining 40% Movement SPD and immunity to Slowing Effects. In this state, the Mecha Sentry will follow the pilot at an increasing speed (can only be controlled by Suppression). Once they meet, Atlas will return to the Mecha, dealing 320 (+80% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemies nearby and stunning them for 0.8s.
Ejected State: Atlas and his Mecha share the same HP bar and reduce 50% of the damage taken in this state.
Skill 4 Description:
Atlas hurls chains around and starts to channel (can only be interrupted by suppressing), dealing 225 (+75% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemy heroes hit and slowing them by 40% for 3s.
Use this skill again while channeling: Atlas will drag the targets toward him and plunk them down on the designated location, dealing 360 (+180% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage.
Use this skill in Ejected State: The Mecha Sentry will return to Atlas immediately, but the stun effect will be replaced by 40% Slowing Effect.

Aulus is a fighter who scales hard with items and extended trades, focusing on front?to?back damage and short?cooldown skirmishes rather than burst all?ins. His kit revolves around stacking Fighting Spirit to boost his Attack Speed and damage, then using The Power of Axe to shred both tanks and squishies while healing through his empowered Basic Attacks. With Aulus, Charge! he can ignore slows, gain front?facing damage reduction, and close gaps reliably, making him very hard to kite once he’s on top of a target.

Aulus fits best in drafts that want a durable, DPS?oriented fighter in the frontline who can both peel and threaten the enemy backline. As his ultimate upgrades his axe over time, he gains more range, penetration, and damage, turning him into a strong mid? to late?game bruiser around objectives and 5v5s. He pairs well with crowd?control supports and tanks that can lock enemies in his burn field and skill range. However, he is vulnerable to hard crowd control and early invades before his items and axe upgrades come online. When played around his scaling and Fighting Spirit windows, Aulus becomes a reliable damage frontliner who can anchor team fights and melt anyone who stands in his path
Basic Attack Description: Aulus adds a stack of Fighting Spirit to his axe per second for 3s after dealing damage to any enemy (up to 3 stacks). Each stack grants 15% extra Attack Speed. Aulus also deals 42-210 extra Physical Damage with his Basic Attacks at max Fighting Spirit stacks (scales with level). The damage counts as Attack Effect.
Skill 1 Description: Aulus removes all Slowing Effects and gains 30% extra Movement Speed and 30% Damage Reduction against attacks from the front for 5s.
Skill 2 Description: Aulus brandishes his axe, dealing 200 (+70% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies in a fan-shaped area and slowing them by 20% for 3s. At max stacks of Fighting Spirit, he deals additional Physical Damage equal to 3.5% of the targets' Max HP. After hitting enemy targets, he enhances his Basic Attacks for 3s. Aulus recovers HP by 50 (+1% Total HP) after each Basic Attack.
Skill 4 Description:
Passive: Every time Undying Fury is upgraded, Aulus crafts a part for his axe in order. Blade Craft: His Basic Attacks deal 50 extra Physical Damage. Handle Craft: Permanently increases his Attack Range by 65% and the range of The Power of Axe. Hammer Craft: Permanently increases his Physical Penetration by 20%.

Active: Aulus raises his axe and smashes it to the ground (this skill can only be interrupted by Suppression), dealing 210 (+100% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies in a line and slowing them by 90% for 0.5s. A burning trail that lasts for 5s is left on the ground, dealing 90 (+40% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies who walk on it every 0.5s and slowing them by 70%.

Note: Aurora is a Magic damage Mage whose Attack Reliance is Crowd Control/Poke, meaning she focuses more on locking enemies down and softening them from range than on pure burst or sustained DPS. Her passive, Pride of Ice, lets her self-freeze instead of dying, becoming invincible for 1.5 seconds and gradually restoring 30% of her Max HP when she would otherwise take fatal damage (with a long cooldown). This makes her especially threatening in siege and team-fight setups: she can stand at a safer distance to poke and control, and even if she’s caught once, Pride of Ice gives her a built?in “second chance” to survive dives and rejoin the fight after her team follows up on her crowd control
Basic Attack Description:
Upon taking fatal damage, Aurora freezes herself for 1.5s, becoming invincible during this time and gradually recovering 30% Max HP. This effect has a 150s cooldown.

Aurora's freeze effects can also affect Turrets.
Skill 1 Description: Aurora summons an icy meteorite to strike at the target location, dealing 400 (+90% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage and slowing targets hit by 40% for 1s. Afterward, 5 hailstones fall, each dealing 40 (+10% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage.
Skill 2 Description: Aurora blows Frosty Breeze in a fan-shaped area in the target direction, dealing 225 (+75% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemies hit, and creating a frozen area at the far-end of the attack that deals a total of 225 (+75% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemies in the area and freezes them for 1s.
Skill 4 Description: Aurora creates a frost path in the target direction, dealing 100 (+40% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemies in the path and reducing their Movement Speed by 80% for 1.2s. The frost path gradually becomes glaciers that spread until reaching their maximum size and shattering, dealing 600 (+150% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to all enemies in the area and freezing targets for 1s. Every 100 Magic Power that Aurora has will increase the freeze duration by 0.2s.

Note: Badang is a fighter who is very strong at locking enemies in place and bursting them down with his wall and punch combo. His kit is most threatening in narrow areas like jungle paths or around objectives, where he can trap targets against his barrier and land multiple enhanced punches for heavy damage. Badang can act as a frontline bruiser who starts fights or follows up on allies’ crowd control to quickly eliminate priority targets. However, he struggles against highly mobile heroes who can dash out of his wall, as well as heavy crowd control and long?range poke that prevent him from getting into melee range. Badang works best with teammates who provide reliable crowd control, additional burst, or displacement to help keep enemies inside his combo zone and secure kills
Basic Attack Description:
Every time Badang's Basic Attack hits a target, he gains a stack of Chivalry Fist. After gaining 4 stacks, his next Basic Attack deals 50 (+30% Total Physical Attack) extra Physical Damage to enemies hit and knocks them back. Enemies that are knocked into obstacles will be stunned for 0.6s (Minions and Creeps are stunned directly).
Fist Wind generated by Badang's skills will trigger this effect directly, and Fist Wind from his Ultimate increases the stun duration to 1s.
Skill 1 Description:
Badang unleashes a gust of Fist Wind in the target direction, dealing 125 (+100% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies hit, slowing them by 30% for 1.5s, and knocking them back. The Fist Wind will explode upon hitting an obstacle, dealing 100 (+60% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to nearby enemies. Fist Wind can trigger attack effects and grants Badang 1 Chivalry Fist stack upon cast.
Badang stores up to 2 Fist Wind charges and restores 1 charge every 8s.
Skill 2 Description:
Badang dashes in the target direction, dealing 230 (+50% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies in his path while gaining a 250 (+150% Total Physical Attack) shield that lasts 3s. He stops immediately upon hitting an enemy hero, slightly knocking them back while creating an obstacle that lasts 4s behind them. Enemies hit by the obstacle are dealt 130 (+30% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage.

Use Again: Badang removes the obstacle he created.
Skill 4 Description:
Badang throws a flurry of punches in the target direction, dealing 60 (+54% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies hit multiple times (can trigger attack effects). The Fist Wind generated by the punches will explode upon hitting an obstacle, dealing 30 (+27% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to nearby enemies.
Badang is immune to control effects for the duration.

Balmond is a durable fighter who excels at early skirmishes, sustained AoE damage, and executing low?HP targets. His kit gives him strong lane presence through HP sustain and spinning damage from Cyclone Sweep, allowing him to clear waves quickly and win extended trades against melee opponents. With decent mobility from Soul Lock and a reliable true?damage execute on Lethal Counter, Balmond can both frontline and secure kills or major objectives like Turtle and Lord.

Balmond fits best in drafts that want a simple, front?to?back team?fight structure with strong objective control. He pairs well with crowd?control supports and tanks that can keep enemies inside his Cyclone Sweep and set up his ultimate for maximum execute value. However, he can be kited by high?mobility backliners and struggles if he falls behind in gold or items. When played around his sustain, cooldowns, and ultimate execution thresholds, Balmond becomes a straightforward but very effective bruiser who converts early leads into secured objectives and team?fight wins.
Basic Attack Description: Balmond recovers 5% Max HP after killing a Minion or Creep, and 20% Max HP after killing a hero.
Skill 1 Description: Balmond charges in the target direction for a set distance or until he hits an enemy hero, dealing 150 (+60% Total Physical Attack)Physical Damage to enemies along the way. The enemy hero hit will be knocked back slightly and slowed by 60% for 2s.
Skill 2 Description: Balmond gains 15% Movement Speed that decays over time and spins with his axe for 3s, dealing 25 (+25% Total Physical Attack)Physical Damage per hit to nearby enemies up to 14 times. Each subsequent hit on the same enemy will deal 8.5% increased damage (up to 68%).The Physical Attack bonus portion of the damage can Crit.
Skill 4 Description: Balmond unleashes a huge strike in the target direction (cannot be interrupted), dealing True Damage equal to 150 (+70% Total Physical Attack) plus 30% of the target's lost HP.This skill only deals up to 1000 damage to non-hero units.

Bane is a flexible fighter/mage who excels at mid?range skirmishes, objective control, and poking enemies down with mixed physical and magic damage. His kit allows him to harass in lane with enhanced Basic Attacks, clear waves quickly, and sustain himself using Ale, while Crab Claw Cannon and his passive let him shred both frontline and backline if left unchecked. With Deadly Catch, Bane also provides powerful zoning and turret pressure, making him a constant threat around Lord, Turtle, and sieges.

Bane fits best in drafts that want strong objective control and siege potential, especially when paired with crowd control or frontliners who can keep enemies inside his AoE damage. He can be built either more physical for burst and tower damage or more magic?focused for heavy spell burst, giving him flexibility to adapt to enemy compositions. However, he lacks hard crowd control and reliable mobility, so he is vulnerable to hard engage and assassins if he mispositions. When played around his cooldowns and item spikes, Bane becomes a dangerous poke/siege core who can quickly turn small leads into destroyed structures and secured objectives.
Basic Attack Description: Bane infuses his weapon with a stack of Tidal Energy each time he uses a skill (up to 2 stacks). Each of his subsequent Basic Attacks consumes a stack to deal Physical Damage (+95% Total Physical Attack) plus 4(+0.4*Hero Level)% of the target's Max HP to nearby enemies.
Skill 1 Description: Bane fires his Crab Claw Cannon in the target direction, dealing 150 (+160% Total Physical Attack)Physical Damage to the first enemy hit and then 150% damage to a random enemy behind them (prioritizes enemy heroes). Enemies hit are slowed by 10 (+10% Total Magic Power)% for 1s. Every 100 Physical Attack Bane possesses reduces this skill's cooldown by an additional 8%.
Skill 2 Description: Bane chugs his ale, recovering 200 (+150% Total Magic Power) plus 5 (+1.5% Total Magic Power)% of his lost HP and gaining 50% extra Movement Speed that decays over 2.5s. Use Again: Bane spits venom in the target direction, dealing 130 (+130% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage (scales up to 250% with charging time) to enemies in a fan-shaped area. Every 100 Magic Power Bane possesses additionally reduces this skill's cooldown by 7%.
Skill 4 Description: Bane summons a school of sharks to charge in the target direction, dealing 700 (+80% Total Physical Attack)(+150% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage to enemies hit, knocking them airborne for 0.6s, and slowing them by 75% (decays over 3s).This skill deals 40% damage to turrets.

Skill 2 Description: Clint shoots a trap net in the target direction, slightly jumping back while dealing 140 (+30% Total Physical Attack) (+150% Total Magic Power)Physical Damage to the first enemy hit and immobilizing them for 1.2s.Successfully hitting an enemy reduces the cooldown of this skill by 40%.
Skill 4 Description: Clint launches a grenade in the target direction that explodes on the first enemy hit, dealing 280 (+100% Total Physical Attack)Physical Damage and slowing them by 50% for 0.5s.Clint gains a grenade charge every 10s (up to 3).

Cyclops is a poke/control mage who excels at sustained spell damage, kiting, and locking down priority targets from mid range. His kit revolves around Starlit Hourglass, which constantly reduces his cooldowns when his skills hit, allowing him to spam abilities and keep enemies under near?permanent pressure. With Stardust Shock and Planets Attack, he can clear waves quickly, harass safely, and force opponents to respect his constant poke before objectives.

Cyclops fits best in drafts that want reliable magic DPS and consistent crowd control rather than all?in burst. His ultimate, Star Power Lockdown, gives his team a dependable single?target immobilize to catch mobile assassins or backline carries, making him valuable in both pick and front?to?back team?fight comps. He pairs well with junglers and tanks who can follow up on his lockdown or help him kite divers trying to reach him. However, he lacks hard mobility and can be punished by heavy dive or long?range burst if he mispositions. When played with good spacing and vision, Cyclops becomes a persistent threat who slowly overwhelms enemies with cooldown resets and nonstop spell pressure.
Basic Attack Description: Each time Cyclops hits an enemy with his skills, all his skill cooldowns are reduced by 0.5s.
Skill 1 Description: Cyclops casts two Stardust Disks in the target direction, each dealing 275 (+60% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage to enemies in its path.
Skill 2 Description: Cyclops conjures Starlit Spheres around himself while gaining 50% Movement Speed that decays over 2s. The spheres will automatically seek and attack nearby enemies (prioritizes enemy heroes), exploding on collision and dealing 200 (+40% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage to the enemy. Enemies hit by multiple spheres will take reduced damage after the first hit.
Skill 4 Description: Cyclops creates a Planetary Sphere and sends it after the target enemy hero or Creep, dealing 500 (+120% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage and immobilizing them for 0.75-1.5s (increases with travel distance).

Note:
Diggie is a support hero who specializes in crowd control, anti?pick, and protecting his teammates from hard CC. His kit revolves around zoning enemies with his bombs, disrupting initiations, and providing safety so his cores can play aggressively. Diggie is especially strong against lineups that rely on hard engage or single?target lockdown to start fights.

Diggie works best with heroes that want to dive in or commit heavily, such as Alpha and other frontliners who need protection from stuns and suppressions. With his ultimate, Diggie can negate crucial enemy control effects, turn losing engages into favorable fights, and give his team confidence to contest objectives without fear of getting instantly caught.
Basic Attack Description: Upon death, Diggie reverses time and turns back to egg form, in which he can continue to move around and gains a new set of skills. He cannot be targeted in egg form and will revive after a period of time.
Skill 1 Description: Diggie flings an owl alarm to the target location that remains stationary for 25s or until it reacts to the first enemy in range, chasing them and exploding upon collision. The explosion deals 350 (+100% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemies hit and slows them by 30%. Diggie gains 2 stacks of Dangerous Sparks each time an enemy hero is hit by the explosion (up to 60 stacks), each stack increasing the skill's damage by 1%. He loses half the stacks upon death, but can gain 1 stack of Dangerous Sparks each time his skill hits an enemy hero when in egg form.Up to 5 owl alarms can exist at the same time.
Skill 2 Description: Diggie marks the target enemy hero for 4s and pulls them back to their previous location after the duration ends, dealing 150 (+100% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage and briefly slowing them by 80%.If the enemy moves out of the circle, the pull will be triggered early.
Skill 4 Description: Diggie removes all debuffs on nearby allied heroes (including himself) and grants them a 650 (+300% Total Magic Power) shield and Control Immunity for 2s. He also gains 50% Movement Speed for 0.5s.

Note:
Dyrroth is an aggressive fighter who excels at shredding frontline targets and dominating extended skirmishes. His kit revolves around stacking his passive to enhance Basic Attacks, reducing enemy defenses, and weaving in skill resets for constant gap closing and damage. With strong lane trading, armor reduction, and a reliable execute on his ultimate, Dyrroth can quickly pressure side lanes and punish tanky heroes who try to stand in front.

Dyrroth fits best in drafts that want a proactive fighter who can dive with the frontline, break through tanks, and clean up low?HP targets. He pairs well with engage supports and crowd?control tanks that can lock enemies in place for his burst windows, as well as lineups that lack %HP or armor?penetration damage from other roles. However, he is vulnerable to heavy crowd control and kiting from ranged carries if he misuses his dashes or overextends without backup. When played with good timing, flanks, and target selection, Dyrroth becomes a high?pressure bruiser who can open fights by softening the frontline and finish them by executing weakened enemies
Basic Attack Description:
When Dyrroth's Rage reaches 50%, he will enhance Burst Strike and Spectre Step.
After every 2 Basic Attacks, Dyrroth will release Circle Strike, dealing (+160% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies in the circle and recovering (20 + 8% of his Max HP) (halved against Minions) (Circle Strike doesn't have Attack Effect). Each time he hits an enemy hero, the cooldown of Burst Strike and Spectre Step will be reduced by 1s.
Skill 1 Description:
Dyrroth releases a burst strike in a designated direction. Each burst deals 200 (+60% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies and slows them by 25% for 1.5s. (The damage decays against the same target and decreases to only 75% on minions.)

Abyss Enhanced: Burst Strike has a longer range, deals 140% of the original damage, and its Slowing Effect is doubled.
Skill 2 Description:
Dyrroth dashes in the designated direction. He will stop when he has traveled the max distance or hits one enemy hero or a Creep, dealing 230 (+60% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to the target and slightly knocking them back. When he uses this skill again, he will lock onto a target and release a Fatal Strike, dealing 345 (+120% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage and reducing the target's Physical Defense by 40% for 4s.
Abyss Enhanced: Fatal Strike will reach further and deal 150% of the original damage, slow the target by an extra 90% and reduce the target's Physical Defense by 60% for 4s.
Skill 4 Description: After a short delay, Dyrroth launches a destructive strike in the target direction (this skill can only be interrupted by Suppression), dealing 650 (+250% Extra Physical Attack) plus 20% of the target's lost HP as Physical Damage to enemies in its path, and slowing them by 55% for 0.8s. This skill deals up to 1500 damage to non-hero enemies.

Edith is a unique tank/marksman hybrid who can switch between a durable front?line mech form and a high?damage ranged carry form. In her Phylax form, she acts as a traditional tank—soaking damage, providing crowd control, and zoning enemies with knock?ups and displacement. After building up enough energy, she can transform into Edith form, gaining range, attack speed, and burst damage to clean up fights from the backline. This dual?form design lets her start fights as a frontliner and then pivot into a temporary DPS threat once the enemy has used key cooldowns.

Edith fits best in drafts that want a flexible frontliner who still contributes meaningful damage, especially in comps that like long skirmishes and front?to?back team fights. She pairs well with supports and junglers who can follow up on her CC in Phylax form and buy time for her to safely output damage in Edith form. However, she can feel underwhelming if her transformations are mistimed, if the team lacks follow?up on her engages, or if the enemy has heavy %HP damage that shreds tanks. When drafted with good peel and coordination, Edith becomes a versatile engage?to?DPS bridge who can both start fights and help finish them
Basic Attack Description: After each skill cast, Edith and Phylax become Overloaded for 3s, during which all Basic Attacks will trigger chain lightning, dealing extra Magic Damage equal to (+20% Total Magic Power) plus 3(+0.2*Hero Level)% of the target's Max HP to up to 4 enemies.Chain lightning damage against Minions is increased to 150%.
Skill 1 Description: After a 0.75s delay, Edith controls Phylax to launch an earth-shattering blow in a designated direction, dealing 225 (+10% Total HP)Physical Damage to enemies hit (deals 120% damage to minions) and knocking them airborne for 0.8s.This skill can only be interrupted by Suppression.
Skill 2 Description: Edith controls Phylax to charge in the target direction, dealing 90 (+3% Total HP)Physical Damage to enemies along the way.If Phylax hits an enemy hero during the charge, it will stop immediately and throw them over its shoulder, dealing 108 (+5% Total HP)Physical Damage
Skill 4 Description: Passive: When inside Phylax, Edith can accumulate Wrath according to the damage she receives (calculated before damage reduction).Active: Edith ejects herself forward from Phylax, knocking back nearby enemies. After that, she takes flight and can perform ranged Basic Attacks, each dealing 35 (+75% Total Physical Attack)(+25% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage. Edith also gains new skills in this state. When in flight, Edith gains 350 (+5% Total HP)-350 (+20% Total HP) extra Shield, 50%-150% extra Attack Speed and 5%-20% Hybrid Lifesteal based on the Wrath she accumulated, and converts each point of Extra Physical Defense and Extra Magic Defense Magic Power. The flight state lasts up to 8s.

Note: Esmeralda is a durable mage–tank who specializes in stealing shields and outlasting enemies in extended fights. Her skills allow her to continuously generate shields for herself while converting enemy shields into her own sustain, making her very hard to burst down if she is allowed to farm and stick to targets. With good positioning, she can dive into the middle of the enemy team, absorb damage, and slowly drain the HP and shields of frontliners and squishy heroes alike. However, she is vulnerable to strong percentage HP damage, anti?shield or anti?regen effects, and hard crowd control that prevents her from freely moving and casting. Esmeralda works best with teammates who provide additional crowd control, frontline presence, and objective pressure so she can take long fights where her shielding and sustain have maximum impact
Basic Attack Description:
Esmeralda manipulates Stardust and Frostmoon: Stardust deals Physical Damage while Frostmoon deals Magic Damage and gives the target a shield equal to 135% of Frostmoon's damage dealt. Each Basic Attack deals (+100% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage and 100 (+75% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage.
The damage dealt by Esmeralda ignores all shield effects and gradually converts her shield into HP.
Skill 1 Description: Esmeralda gains 400 (+150% Total Magic Power) Shield and 40% Movement Speed which rapidly decays over its duration for 4s. Meanwhile, she gradually transforms the shields of her nearby enemies into her own shield, capped at 50% of her Max HP.
Skill 2 Description: Esmeralda waves Stardust and Frostmoon, dealing 240 (+60% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage and 300 (+120% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to nearby enemies. Each time she deals damage to a hero, the cooldown of Frostmoon Shield is reduced by 1.5s (damaging non-hero units grants a 0.5s reduction) and the enemy's Movement Speed is reduced by 10% for 1.5s.
Skill 4 Description:
Esmeralda coheres the power of Astrospace into her two weapons - Stardust and Frostmoon. The longer this skill is channeled, the longer the cast range.

Use Again: Esmeralda casts Stardust at the target location, dealing 350 (+90% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage, and then blinks to the target location and casts Frostmoon, dealing 350 (+140% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage and immobilizing enemies in the area for 1s.

Estes is a pure support healer who excels at keeping his team alive in extended fights and stabilizing skirmishes that would otherwise be lost. His kit revolves around strong single?target and AoE healing, plus slows and basic crowd control that help kite enemies and protect his carries. With his ultimate active, Estes can massively boost his team’s sustain in 5v5s, allowing them to outlast enemy burst as long as they stay within his healing radius and position around him properly.

Estes fits best in team compositions that want to group early, force coordinated fights, and play front?to?back around durable tanks or hyper?carries. He pairs extremely well with comps that lack self?sustain but have strong DPS, enabling them to keep dealing damage while he handles the defensive side. However, he is vulnerable to hard engage, anti?heal, and dive that bypasses the frontline to reach him or his backline. When drafted into lineups that can front line for him and itemize against Grievous Wounds/anti?regen, Estes becomes a powerful backbone of team fights who turns every extended battle into a war of attrition his team is favored to win
Passive Description:
Estes mengisi energi secara bertahap seiring waktu.

Ketika energi penuh, basic attack Estes memberikan tambahan magic damage ke target utama dan musuh di sekitarnya.

Basic attack yang terisi energi juga memberikan efek slow pada musuh yang terkena, memperlambat pergerakan mereka.

Passive ini mendukung Estes untuk tidak hanya sebagai healer, tetapi juga memiliki kontribusi damage dan crowd control ringan melalui basic attack-nya saat energi passive aktif. Ini membuat Estes cukup berguna dalam pertarungan tim sekaligus menjaga jarak dengan mengurangi kecepatan musuh
Basic Attack Description: Scripture of the Moon Elf slowly charges Estes with energy. when the energy reaches 100 stacks, Estes' next Basic Attack will become enhanced dealing 250(+100 Total Physical attack) (+150% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to the target and 125 (+50% total physical attack)(+75% total magic power)Magic Damage to nearby enemies and slowing them by 60% for 1.5s
Skill 1 Description: Estes restores 250(+110% Total magic power) HP to the target allied hero immediately and links himself with them for 3s, slowly restoring 325 (+60% Total Magic Power) HP to the target. Linking with an allied hero will also increase estes' hybrid defense by 20 and movement speed by 15%, as well as the energy charging speed of the scripture of the moon elf. being too far from the target will break the link.
Skill 2 Description: Estes drops a flood of moonlight on the target area. dealing 350(+70% total magic power) Magic Damage to enemy units within it. Afterwards, it turns into a Domain of the Moon Goddess and reveals enemies inside it. Enemies will be slowed by 90% for 1.5s if they touch the edge of the domain area.(The slow effect will decay over time)
Skill 4 Description: Estes casts an enhanced Moonlight Immersion on all nearby allied heroes. within the next 8s. Moonlight immersion will be enhanced and estes will continuously recover 1230 (+210% total magic power) HP.

Eudora is a classic burst mage who specializes in point?and?click damage and reliable single?target pick potential. Her kit revolves around stacking her passive to amplify damage, then using her quick combo of stun plus follow?up skills to instantly delete squishy targets before they can react. With simple but very high front?loaded damage, she is especially threatening in fog of war, brushes, and tight jungle paths where enemies have limited time to dodge or disengage.

Eudora fits best in drafts that want straightforward, easy?to?execute pick and burst compositions. She pairs extremely well with tanks or supports that can provide vision, lockdown, or peel so she can safely step into range, stun a priority target, and complete her combo. However, she lacks mobility and sustained damage, making her vulnerable to long fights, heavy poke, or assassins that can dodge her initial stun and collapse on her. When drafted with good frontline and engage, Eudora becomes a simple but very effective answer to fragile backliners and immobile mages who misposition even once
Basic Attack Description: Eudora's skills inflict Superconductor for 3s on hit and can trigger additional effects against enemies affected by Superconductor
Skill 1 Description: Eudora casts forked lightning in the target direction, dealing 350 (+150% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage to enemies in a fan-shaped area.Enemies affected by Superconductor will take 190 (+30% Total Magic Power) extra Magic Damage after a short delay.
Skill 2 Description: Eudora hurls an orb of lightning at the target enemy, dealing 350 (+80% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage, stunning them for 1.2s, and reducing their Magic Defense by 10 for 1.8s.If the enemy is affected by Superconductor, the lightning orb will bounce to up to 3 nearby enemies (prioritizes enemy heroes), dealing 175 (+40% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage and stunning them for 0.9s.
Skill 4 Description: Eudora calls down a blast of lightning on the target enemy, dealing 480 (+180% Total Magic Power)Magic DamageIf the enemy is affected by Superconductor, dark clouds appear over their head and unleash an additional lightning strike on the area after 0.8s, dealing 440 (+150% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage to enemies within and 360 (+150% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage to nearby enemies.

Note: Fanny is a high-mobility Physical Assassin who specializes in rapid engages and burst damage through her cable mechanics. Her passive, Air Superiority, lets her deal increased damage while flying and apply Prey Marks that refund energy when she hits marked enemy heroes with her skills, rewarding precise and aggressive play. Tornado Strike provides close-range AoE damage as she spins her blades, while Steel Cable is the core of her kit, allowing her to dash between walls, automatically triggering Tornado Strike on enemies mid-flight when she has enough energy and enabling creative paths and sudden picks. Her ultimate, Cut Throat, delivers a powerful single-target execute whose damage scales heavily with the number of Prey Marks, making fully marked squishy targets extremely vulnerable. Fanny is very hard to master and heavily dependent on energy management, map awareness, and wall usage, but in the right hands she can quickly eliminate priority targets and dominate chaotic fights.
Basic Attack Description: During flight, Fanny deals 10%-20% extra damage to enemies hit (scales with flying speed) and applies a stack of Prey Mark to them (up to 2 stacks) on each attack. Her subsequent skill hits on marked enemy heroes restore 8 energy per stack for her. The energy restoration is reduced if she hits multiple enemy heroes within a short period of time.
Skill 1 Description: Fanny whirls her blades, dealing 275 (+85% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage to nearby enemies.
Skill 2 Description:
Fanny shoots a cable in the target direction that pulls her to the first obstacle hit. She can cast this skill again within 2s until her energy runs out. Each successive cast reduces the skill's energy cost by 2.

Fanny automatically casts Tornado Strike upon hitting an enemy mid-flight, as long as her energy is sufficient.
Skill 4 Description: Fanny leaps at the target enemy hero or Creep with her blades, dealing 400 (+200% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage. Each stack of Prey Mark on the target increases this damage by 30%.

Note:
Faramis is a support/mage who excels at turning chaotic team fights in his team’s favor through revives, area control, and sustained magic damage. His kit revolves around gathering soul fragments to increase his power, disrupting enemy positioning with Shadow Stampede pulls, and spreading damage across multiple targets with Ghost Bursters. In extended fights around objectives, Faramis becomes increasingly dangerous as he collects more fragments and keeps enemies trapped in his damage zones.

Faramis works best with lineups that want to hard engage or fight in tight spaces, such as compositions built around frontliners like Baxia, Thamuz, or other dive heroes. With Nether Realm, he can give his team a powerful pseudo?revive and extra HP, allowing them to commit deeper, absorb enemy ultimates, and re?enter the fight while the enemy has already spent key cooldowns. In the right team, Faramis can completely change how risky engages feel, enabling aggressive, high?tempo playstyles
Basic Attack Description: Every 4s, Faramis' next skill against enemy heroes and summoned objects generates a soul fragment on the spot. Faramis can absorb the soul fragment to restore 100 (+50% Total Magic Power) HP and gain 2 extra Magic Power (up to 40 stacks). Upon death, he consumes the absorbed soul fragments to reduce the respawn timer, each reducing the timer by 3% (up to 90%). Enemies that die around Faramis also have a chance to drop soul fragments.
Skill 1 Description:
Faramis enters the Shadow state for 3s, gaining 70% extra Movement Speed, 25 extra Physical & Magic Defense, 20% cooldown reduction of this skill, and the ability to move through terrain. Enemy heroes that come into contact with Faramis in this state are dealt 250 (+60% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage and applied with a Nether Mark. Upon leaving the Shadow state, Faramis drags all the marked enemy heroes toward him, dealing 250 (+60% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage. Use again to leave the Shadow state early and drag marked enemies toward him.
The range of soul fragment absorption is increased while this skill is active.
Skill 2 Description: Faramis gathers Nether energy in a fan-shaped area ahead, dealing 330 (+144% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage to enemies within. The energy will then split and bounce to nearby enemies, dealing 200 (+86% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage (splits up to 2 time(s) on enemy hero hits and 1 time(s) on non-enemy hero hits).
Skill 4 Description: Faramis turns his surroundings into the Nether Realm for 6s, making affected allied heroes (including himself) enter the Specter state and granting them 400 plus 10 (+5% Total Magic Power)% extra HP and 50% extra Movement Speed for 1s. When the Specter state breaks, the hero will clear all debuffs and enter a brief Resurrection state for 1.3s. An allied hero's Specter state ends when they leave the Nether Realm.

Note:
Floryn is a backline support who focuses on healing, shielding, and empowering her teammates rather than dealing damage herself. Her kit revolves around providing sustained sustain, global healing, and utility from a safe distance, allowing her cores to play more aggressively without constantly recalling. With her shared item mechanic and teamwide buffs, Floryn scales well into mid and late game, especially in coordinated team fights around objectives.

Floryn works best with heroes that want to dive in or stay in the middle of fights for a long time, such as fighters and frontliners like Baxia, Alpha, or Thamuz, as well as fragile hypercarries that need protection. In the right lineup, she can keep her front line alive through heavy burst, stabilize chaotic skirmishes with clutch global heals, and turn losing fights around by extending how long her team can stay on the map without giving up tempo
Basic Attack Description:
Dew's Lantern will permanently increase Floryn's attributes by a small amount.

After leaving combat for 5s, Floryn can share the Flower of Hope with an allied hero (30s cooldown), which will grant them a 100 (+70% Total Magic Power) shield each time they are healed by Floryn.

Floryn will never sell the Lantern
Skill 1 Description: Floryn tosses an Energy Seed at the target enemy, dealing 180 (+100% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage. Healing Fruits will then spawn and bounce to nearby allied heroes, restoring their HP by 175 (+90% Total Magic Power)
Skill 2 Description: Floryn casts a blob of energy ahead that explodes upon hitting an enemy, dealing 175 (+90% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage to nearby enemies and stunning them for 0.5s (and revealing their positions briefly).
Skill 4 Description: Floryn resonates with Dew's power, restoring 250 (+100% Total Magic Power)HP to all allied heroes 2 times no matter where they are. This effect also increases their Shield and HP Regen by 12% for 2s.

Note:
Franco is a hard?engage tank who specializes in picks, single?target lockdown, and front?line disruption. His kit revolves around threatening long?range hooks with Iron Hook, forcing enemies to constantly respect his positioning and the fog of war. Once he lands a hook, Franco can immediately follow up with Fury Shock and Bloody Hunt to suppress and burst a priority target, often deleting them with his team before the fight truly begins. Outside of picks, his high base durability and AoE slow let him peel effectively and soak damage on the front line.

Franco fits best in drafts that want simple, pick?oriented engage tools and strong early–mid game pressure. He pairs extremely well with burst mages and high?damage marksmen who can instantly follow up on a successful hook or ultimate. He is especially powerful in comps that play around vision control, brush setups, and objective traps. However, Franco can struggle into highly mobile backliners, comps with strong disengage, or teams that group tightly and position well behind minions. When drafted with good follow?up damage and vision, Franco becomes a constant threat on the map, turning any misstep into a numbers advantage and forcing the enemy team to play cautiously at all times
Basic Attack Description: If no damage is taken within 5s, Franco gains 10% Movement Speed, recovers 1% Max HP per second, and begins accumulating Wasteland Force (up to 10 stacks).Franco will consume all Wasteland Force stacks on his next skill cast to increase the skill's damage by up to 150%.
Skill 1 Description: Franco launches an iron hook in the target direction. The hook will snag the first enemy unit hit, dealing 400 (+100% Total Physical Attack)Physical Damage and dragging them to Franco.
Skill 2 Description: Franco lashes out, dealing Physical Damage equal to 300 plus 4% of his Max HP to nearby enemies and slowing them by 70% for 1.5s.
Skill 4 Description: Franco suppresses the target enemy hero for 1.8s and strikes them 6 times over the duration, each time dealing 50 (+70% Total Physical Attack)Physical Damage

Note:
Fredrinn is a front?line fighter/tank who specializes in layered crowd control, damage conversion, and outlasting enemies in extended fights. His kit revolves around building up Combo Points and using skills in sequence to unlock stronger versions and a powerful finisher, letting him trade aggressively while staying surprisingly durable. With a mix of displacement, taunt, and damage?to?shield mechanics, Fredrinn can both peel for his backline and dive into the enemy team to disrupt their formation.

Fredrinn fits best in team compositions that want a durable engage/peel hybrid who can front line confidently and buy time for carries. He pairs well with sustained DPS marksmen or mages who can take advantage of the space he creates and the targets he locks down. While he is hard to burst and scales well in skirmishes, he can struggle against heavy %HP damage or comps that completely ignore him and dive past his front line. When piloted with good combo management and positioning, Fredrinn becomes a reliable anchor who soaks damage, controls key targets, and turns long fights in his team’s favor.
Passive Description:
Fredrinn gains 1 Combo Point that lasts 5s each time his skill hits a non-minion enemy, up to 4 Combo Points. His Ultimates cost different numbers of Combo Points.

Fredrinn stores 100% of the damage he receives as Crystal Energy, which decays after 5s at a rate of 10% Max HP per second.
Fredrinn can convert the stored Crystal Energy into HP by 20% of his damage dealt (10% for damage dealt to minions). Gaining a Combo Point resets the decaying timer.
Basic Attack Description:
Fredrinn thrusts his sword in the target direction, dealing 125 (+7% Total HP) (+120% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies hit and slowing them by 30% for 2s. His next Basic Attack gains extra attack range and deals 85 (+100% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage.
This skill deals 200% damage to non-hero enemies.
Skill 1 Description: Fredrinn dashes in the target direction, dealing 140 (+80% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to the first non-minion enemy hit. His next Basic Attack knocks the target airborne for 0.3s.
Skill 2 Description:
Fredrinn deals 210 (+100% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to nearby enemies and taunts them for 1s. Hitting a non-minion enemy grants Fredrinn 25 Physical & Magic Defense for 3s and reduces the cooldowns of Piercing Strike and Brave Assault by 75%.
This skill costs 1 Combo Point.
Skill 4 Description:
Fredrinn slams his sword in the target direction (this skill can only be interrupted by Suppression), dealing 600 plus 21% of his Crystal Energy as Physical Damage to enemies in a fan-shaped area after a short delay. Enemies in the center of the area take 175% damage. This skill doubles the conversion ratio based on damage dealt to enemy heroes from stored Crystal Energy to HP.
This skill costs 3 Combo Points.

Note: Freya is a fighter who relies on jumping into the middle of fights, using her shields and empowered basic attacks to trade aggressively at close range. Her kit gives her strong single-target lockdown and burst during her ultimate, allowing her to quickly pressure squishy heroes or frontline targets that stand too close. With items, Freya can become very durable while still dealing meaningful damage, making her a constant threat in skirmishes and small teamfights. However, she is vulnerable to kiting, hard crowd control, and heroes that can out-sustain or out-range her before she gets into melee range. Freya works best with teammates who provide reliable engage, additional crowd control, or peel so she can safely dive in, stick to her targets, and avoid being focused down too early in the fight.
Basic Attack Description:
Freya gains 1 Sacred Orb with each Basic Attack (up to 6 Sacred Orbs). Consuming 1 Sacred Orb grants Freya 100% Attack Speed for her next Basic Attack (max 6 stacks).
Sacred Orbs gradually recover when out of combat.
Skill 1 Description: Freya leaps to the target area and strikes the ground with her shield, gaining 500 (+100% Total Physical Attack) shield and dealing 200 (+80% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies within while knocking them airborne for 0.4s.
Skill 2 Description:
Freya charges forward and slashes, dealing 150 (+50% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage and slowing enemies by 30% for 0.5s. This skill has no base cooldown but consumes 2 Sacred Orbs per cast.
This skill deals 50% damage to Creeps.
Skill 4 Description: Freya selects a target area and dives down as a Sacred Orb, dealing 300 (+75% Total Physical Attack) Physical Damage and 40% slow to enemies in her path and at the landing point for 2s. Upon landing, Freya enters the Valkyrie state for 12s, during which her Basic Attacks deal 30 extra damage (extra damage cannot Crit) and she recovers 60 (+40% Total Physical Attack) HP per Basic Attack, and her Basic Attacks deal splash damage.

Note:
Gatotkaca is a durable tank/fighter who specializes in hard engage, damage absorption, and disruptive crowd control. His kit revolves around jumping into the middle of the enemy team, soaking damage through his passive damage?to?defense conversion, and locking multiple targets in place so his allies can freely follow up. With his strong taunt, slows, and knock?ups, Gatotkaca can repeatedly force enemies to fight on his terms and make it difficult for them to ignore him or bypass the frontline.

Gatotkaca works best with heroes who can quickly capitalize on his initiation, such as burst mages, marksmen, or fighters like Alpha, Thamuz, or Terizla who want enemies grouped together. When paired with strong AoE damage or follow?up crowd control, his ultimate can start devastating team fights, allowing his team to wipe clustered opponents or secure key objectives. In the right lineup, Gatotkaca acts as both a primary engager and a reliable frontliner who creates space and safety for his backline
Basic Attack Description: Gatotkaca gains Physical Defense equal to 2% of his lost HP (up to 200). For every 300 damage he takes (calculated before damage reduction), he gains 5 Rage (up to 100). Upon reaching over 25 Rage, Gatotkaca's next Basic Attack becomes enhanced, consuming all Rage to deal extra Magic Damage  and recover HP. The extra damage scales with his Rage, level, and Magic Power.
Skill 1 Description: Gatotkaca slams the ground, creating a shattered zone in the target direction while dealing 200  (+150% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage  to enemies within. Enemies in the shattered zone will take 100 (+20% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage  per second and be slowed by 30%.
Skill 2 Description: Gatotkaca begins channeling, then sprints in the target direction with a battle cry, forcing enemies on the path to attack him and deal 200 (+100% Total Magic Power) Magic Damage  for 1.5s. The sprint distance scales with the channel time. Canceling the Skill reduces 50% of the remaining Cooldown.
Skill 4 Description: Gatotkaca jumps to the target location, dealing 500 (+300% Total Magic Power)Magic Damage to nearby enemies and knocking them airborne for 1s. Enemies near the center of the area will be knocked airborne for a longer duration, while enemies on the fringes will be pulled to the center. The camera will move with the skill indicator but won't grant extra sight.
